entries.test: Public evaluations of 2019–early 2023 LLMs on novel event sequences could establish whether they reliably track temporal order and resulting world states across varied formulations.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives robust world models a concrete reading: reliable reasoning about how events unfold.

entries.test: Public controlled studies adding or removing temporal world representations could test whether their absence explains the cited errors and is the principal source of such failures.
entries.note: This asserts a causal explanation; error examples alone would not establish it.
The proposition broadens a contextual claim about persistent reasoning flaws into general fundamental continuity. Fundamental change has no shared test without specifying the dimension.

entries.test: Public comparisons of GPT-2 and early-2023 GPT outputs could measure fluency improvements and whether numerous previously documented errors were corrected.
entries.note: The comparison with GPT-2 in 2019 is supplied by the surrounding text.

entries.test: Archived outputs and reproducible evaluations of ChatGPT after its January 30, 2023 update could establish whether it frequently failed easy word problems.
entries.note: The embedded examples supply the update date and identify ChatGPT as the target.
Understanding what it is talking about has no shared operational test here. The cited reasoning failures illustrate his concern but do not define understanding.
